step4.objective:
• All optional TLVs available in the LLDP TLV set — port description, system name, system description, system capabilities and management address — are individually selectable and individually clearable on a per-port basis.
  • Selecting the complete set of optional TLVs on a transmitting port results in every selected TLV being present in each transmitted LLDPDU, in addition to the mandatory TLVs.
  • With LLDP enabled and no optional TLVs selected, transmitted LLDPDUs carry only the mandatory TLVs (chassis ID, port ID, time-to-live) and the end-of-LLDPDU marker, and no optional TLV appears on the wire.
  • Each single-instance optional TLV appears at most once in any single LLDPDU — no LLDPDU carries duplicate port description, system name, system description or system capabilities TLVs.
  • At least one management address TLV is present in every transmitted LLDPDU when management address transmission is selected; where multiple management addresses are associated with the port, multiple management address TLVs may be carried in one LLDPDU.
  • Management address TLV contents reflect the management address actually configured on the device, and change to match when that address changes.
  • The content of every transmitted TLV matches the corresponding locally configured or locally derived value as reported by the device's own management interfaces.
  • The per-port TLV transmit-enable state held in the LLDP management information base agrees with the state selected through the command interface, port by port and TLV by TLV.
  • Per-port independence holds: TLV selections applied to one port do not alter the TLVs transmitted on any other port, including ports with no optional TLVs selected.
  • Optional TLV selection takes effect on a transmit-only port with the same result as on a transmit-and-receive port; receive capability is not a precondition for TLV transmission.
  • The LLDP-MED TLV set is separately selectable from the basic optional TLV set, and MED TLV selections are reflected in transmitted LLDPDUs as the standards-defined organisationally specific TLVs.
  • MED capability and network policy TLV contents conform to the defined TLV format and carry values consistent with the device's MED configuration.
  • Selecting or clearing a TLV while LLDP is running takes effect on subsequent LLDPDUs without requiring LLDP or the port to be restarted, and without disrupting transmission of the remaining TLVs.
  • An attempt to select an unsupported, misspelled or out-of-range TLV keyword is rejected with a diagnostic message, and the previously configured TLV selection is left unchanged.
  • TLV selection commands on a port with LLDP disabled are accepted and retained as configuration, and become effective when LLDP is subsequently enabled.
  • Repeating a selection already in effect, or clearing a TLV that is already deselected, is accepted without error and leaves the resulting state unchanged.
  • TLV selection state is reported by the device's operational display commands, per port, distinguishing selected from unselected TLVs.
  • TLV selection state appears in the saved and displayed running configuration in a form that restores the same selections after a device restart.
  • A neighbour device receiving the LLDPDUs reports exactly the set of optional TLVs selected on the transmitting port, and reports no information for TLVs that were not selected.
  • LLDP frame and TLV counters remain consistent across TLV selection changes, with no increment of error, malformed-frame or discarded-TLV counters attributable to a valid TLV selection.
